page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.large is an x86_64 cloud server instance within the c8i-flex family, running on AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 1 physical CPU core split across 2 virtual CPUs with burstable CPU allocation. Hardware capability includes 4.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 7 GHz (2.0 GB per core), a 480 MB L3 cache, and instruction set support including AVX-512, Intel AMX, AES, and SHA extensions. The instance includes no attached local NVMe storage, zero baseline network bandwidth, and no GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results reveal a notable split between single-core and multi-threaded performance. In single-core testing, the instance exhibits strong performance, scoring 2164.0 on Geekbench single-core, achieving 34.07 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, and 14.14 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, due to its limitation of 1 physical core (2 vCPUs) and burstable CPU allocation, overall multi-core throughput is constrained, registering a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2700.0 and a poor stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 2164.08. Uncached memory bandwidth metrics remain weak to poor (20.61 GB/sec read and 17.05 GB/sec write), reflecting memory throughput constraints under heavy workloads.

Positioned as an entry-level burstable compute instance, c8i-flex.large provides high single-threaded performance for light or variable compute profiles without the high cost of full dedicated core allocations. The configuration is suitable for light web microservices, basic text processing, single-threaded batch compression tasks, and development or testing environments requiring modern x86 instruction support like AMX and AVX-512. It is less suitable for sustained multi-threaded execution, memory-intensive databases, or large-scale data processing due to its minimal memory capacity and low multi-core benchmark outcomes.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.large is a burstable compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture with AWS Nitro hypervisor management. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, it features 1 physical core yielding 2 virtual CPUs, 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory, and a 480 MB L3 cache. Advanced instructions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX are supported. The instance includes no attached local storage or baseline network bandwidth allocations. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-threaded throughput, achieving high scores in single-core Geekbench tests and single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-threaded CPU performance and uncached memory bandwidth fall into weak or poor tiers due to the single physical core limit and burstable allocation mode. This instance is best suited for burstable light web microservices, single-threaded text or compression tasks, and lightweight development workloads.
